title: go-sdk: streaming degrader and cancellation-throttle patterns for resilient client churn
creator: Ava Patel
description: Investigate and implement a set of patterns in the Go SDK streaming stack to mitigate client churn and rapid cancellation storms. The goal is to avoid head-of-line blocking, reduce wasted GPU work, and provide ergonomic primitives for callers to opt into early-ack, graceful teardown, and cancellation-throttling behavior. Deliver a backward-compatible API surface with examples and tests.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a small opt-in Degrader API (EarlyAck + ThrottleHint) that prevents repeated goroutine churn under rapid cancel/reattach patterns
Server-facing and client-facing examples demonstrate <20% additional CPU under synthetic cancellation flood compared to baseline
No regression in existing streaming semantics: clients that don't opt-in behave exactly as today
Unit and integration tests cover cancellation races, delayed resume, and kv-cache interaction
Bench dashboard (internal) reports token-level wasted-work and request-latency before/after change
design_notes: Observed issue: bursty client churn causes repeated start/stop of in-flight model context and large amounts of wasted CPU on token generation. Existing cancel handling tears down compute without coordination which overloads connection supervisor when many clients reconnect.

Trade-offs considered: 1) server-side queueing to debounce reconnects (adds server latency); 2) client-side backoff (burdens integrators); 3) SDK-level degrade + throttle (picked) because it localizes complexity and enables ergonomic defaults.

Chosen pattern: implement a lightweight 'Degrader' that can optionally return an early ACK (stream-level metadata event) and then hold a short grace window for retries before fully cancelling downstream compute. A separate cancellation-throttle gate prevents N cancellations per-second from the same client connection.
Compatibility: feature is opt-in via ClientStreamOpts{Degrader: &DegraderConfig{Enabled:true, GraceMs:200, MaxCancelsPerMinute:30}} so existing users unaffected.
Observability: emit events to SDK telemetry: sdk.stream.degrader.ack, sdk.stream.degrader.expire, sdk.stream.cancel.throttled. Add counters and sample traces to trace plumbing.

Interaction with KV cache & batching: when degrader defers full cancellation, it must maintain the request's cache key semantics. We avoid holding expensive KV locks by switching to a 'soft-hold' that preserves prefix cache state but yields on heavy memory pressure. Runtime will surface a metric when soft-hold is evicted.
implementation_tasks: Add DegraderConfig struct and default values into go-sdk stream client package
Implement degrader state machine (ACK -> GraceTimer -> Expire/PromoteCancel) with lock-free counters for throttle enforcement
Add graceful-shutdown hook so that when the client process terminates we still flush minimal end-of-stream event
Integrate telemetry counters and traces: sdk.stream.degrader.* and sdk.stream.cancel.*
Add compatibility layer to ensure non-opt-in streams have zero overhead (compile-time flag checked at hot-path)
Update examples: examples/streaming/degrader_demo.go and README snippet showing opt-in and rationale
Create integration harness that simulates 1000 clients with 50% cancellation churn and measure wasted-token work
Add unit tests for state transitions and deterministic timeouts using clock injection
Open PR with implementation and link to docs and perf dashboard
testing_plan: Unit tests for Degrader state transitions and throttle counters (deterministic clocks)
Integration test: local runner that starts 200 parallel streams and issues random cancellation bursts, assert success rate and wasted-work metric
Load test in staging: run synthetic workload with configured GPU cluster and compare token-cost, tail-latency against control branch
Fuzz test: simulate rapid connect/cancel/connect sequences to surface races
E2E check: examples compile and run; official README snippet verified
Canary rollout: feature flag gated and enabled for 5% of traffic in dedicated environment before full roll
